sanskrit: अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः ।
translit: anye cha bahavaḥ śhūrā madarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ
theme: Many Loyal Heroes Stand Beside Me
hindi: दुर्योधन कहता है: और भी बहुत से शूरवीर हैं, जिन्होंने मेरे लिए अपने जीवन की आशा छोड़ दी है। वे सब तरह-तरह के शस्त्र चलाने वाले हैं और युद्ध की कला में बहुत निपुण हैं।
english: Duryodhana tells Drona: “There are many other brave warriors too, who are ready to give up their lives for my sake. They carry many kinds of weapons, and all of them are skilled in battle.”
deeper: After naming the famous warriors in verse 8, Duryodhana adds “and many others.” He wants Drona to feel that his army is not only big but also loyal, brave and well trained. Every word is meant to build confidence.

Notice the words “for my sake.” Duryodhana speaks of others’ courage as if it belongs to him. A good leader is grateful for the people who stand by him and cares for them. Someone who only counts on them may be hiding his own worry.

The verse also teaches that strength has three parts: loyalty (people who stand with you), variety (many kinds of weapons and skills), and training (being expert at what you do). Having all three is wonderful, but the Gita will soon show that even a strong army cannot give peace to a heart that is not right.
words: ready to give up their lives
armed with many kinds of weapons
background: The two armies stand ready at Kurukshetra. Duryodhana, the Kaurava prince, goes to his teacher Drona and points out the Pandava army (1.2–1.3). He names their great warriors, such as Yudhamanyu, Uttamauja, Abhimanyu and the sons of Draupadi (1.6).

Then he says he will name the leaders on his own side (1.7). In verse 8 he lists Drona, Bhishma, Karna, Kripa, Ashvatthama, Vikarna and Saumadatti. Now, in verse 9, he adds that many more warriors are ready to give up their lives for him.
lessons: Those who stand by you, like family, friends and teachers, are a great blessing, so thank them.
Being “skilled in battle” comes from training, and every skill we admire comes from hard work.
Many kinds of weapons remind us that a team needs many kinds of talents.
Do not use people only for yourself
“For my sake” is a warning: a good leader cares for his people and does not just count on them.
Numbers cannot calm a worried heart
Duryodhana keeps counting his helpers, yet he still feels unsure, because real confidence comes from doing right.
examples: Before the match, Rohan’s captain looks around and smiles. Eleven players are ready, and a few more are waiting as substitutes. Knowing the team is ready makes everyone feel braver.
Ananya is the best at maths quizzes because she solves two sums every evening. Skill does not come by luck. It comes from practice, just like the warriors who were “skilled in battle.”
Meera’s parents wake up early every day to pack her lunch and get her to school. She decides to say “thank you” each morning. People who work for us deserve our gratitude.
For the school exhibition, one friend paints, one writes, and one builds the model. Everyone uses a different tool, and the project turns out wonderful.
Karan’s group project is not finished, and three friends stay after school to help. Karan says, “You are all so kind,” and does not treat their help as something he is owed.
Aarav is nervous about his stage speech, so he keeps counting how many friends are in the audience. Then his teacher tells him, “Be calm and prepare your heart, too.” True courage grows inside us.
Sana is the kabaddi captain. At practice she checks that every teammate has water and is not hurt. A good leader looks after the people who work with him.
In Grandfather’s workshop, Dev learns that a hammer, a saw and a screwdriver each have a job. Having many tools helps only if you know how to use each one well.

story.title: Captain Meera and the Village Cricket Team
paras: In a small village near Nashik, eleven-year-old Meera was captain of the school cricket team. Before the big final, she stood in the field and looked at her team. Pranav bowled fast, Salma was a brilliant fielder, and Gopal could hit sixes. “With a team like this, we will win!” she thought proudly.

Then Meera noticed something. Her friends had given up their games and holidays to practise with her for weeks. Meera had been saying “my team” all week, as if they were hers to command. Suddenly she felt a little embarrassed.

She called everyone together. “Friends, you have all worked so hard and given up so much. This is not my team, it is our team. Win or lose, thank you for standing with me.” Everybody cheered, and the team felt warm and happy.

They played with joy and lost by just two runs. But nobody cried. Pranav said, “We played well together,” and the whole team had ice-cream afterwards. Meera felt that day she had become a true captain.
story.moral: Lesson: Loyal friends are a gift, not a possession. Thank them, care for them, and remember that real strength is not only in counting people but in being fair and kind to them.

quiz.q: What does Duryodhana say about the many other warriors on his side?
o: They are afraid of the battle
They are ready to give up their lives for him
quiz.x: He says they are “madarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ,” ready to give up their lives for his sake.
Viśhāradāḥ means skilled or expert, and yuddha means battle.

quiz.q: What does “nānā-śhastra” (many kinds of weapons) remind us about teams?
o: Everyone should do the same thing
A team needs many different skills
Weapons are more important than people
quiz.x: Different tools and talents together make a team strong.

quiz.q: What gentle warning is hidden in the words “for my sake”?
o: A good leader should care for people, not just rely on them
quiz.x: Leaders should be grateful to those who stand by them and look after their well-being.

reel.hook: Duryodhana counts his helpers again. Why does he still feel worried?
reel.lesson: Loyal friends are a gift: thank them and care for them.
reel.caption:
Many brave helpers stood beside Duryodhana, but a good leader must also care for them. 🛡️
Who helps you every day? Say thank you today! 💛
Gita for kids, one verse at a time.
